title: add-interactive-multimodal-progressive-streaming-quickstart
author: Sana Patel
description: Introduce a new quickstart that demonstrates a lightweight multimodal RAG flow with progressive token/image streaming, client-side incremental preview, and an automatic fallback to chunked (non-streaming) responses for environments that do not support streaming sockets. The quickstart includes TypeScript browser preview, a Python worker example that shows how to orchestrate text+image retrieval and tool calls, a small instrumentation guide for Redwood Console (telemetry hooks, token cost breakdown), and a short troubleshooting section for common connectivity and CORS issues. Motivation: customers building blended text+image assistants need an approachable reference that covers both UX patterns (live partial output, image-by-image progressive renders) and server-side patterns (KV cache snapshots across multimodal contexts, progressive decoding hooks). This PR bundles docs, runnable samples, CI tests, and a minimal e2e scenario to validate fallback behavior.

release_notes: Add multimodal progressive-streaming quickstart: includes browser preview (TS), Python worker sample, e2e test for streaming->fallback behavior, and docs with telemetry guidance.
notes_for_operators: This quickstart touches the streaming client surface; operators should verify that their load balancers allow long-lived connections or ensure the provided chunked fallback is enabled. The README includes an nginx example for proxy timeouts and an H2 vs WS compatibility table.
testing_instructions: 1) Run the Python worker sample: python examples/python/worker/streaming_adapter.py --mock-index; 2) Start the TS preview (yarn && yarn dev) and open /preview; 3) Toggle 'simulate network block' to exercise fallback; 4) Observe Redis KV snapshots under keys quickstart:multimodal:session:* and verify token-count traces in Console.
manual_backport_considerations: Not required. This is a docs/examples-only change and does not touch runtime binaries. If backporting to release branches for customer onboarding, include only the README and examples folders; skip CI workflow updates.
